2016_096_062116mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education met on June 21, 2016, opening with a public hearing on the proposed 2016/2017 budget presented by Assistant Superintendent Rick West. The appropriations resolution sets a General Fund appropriation of $142,948,405 and authorizes 18.0000 mills on non-homestead property, 5.6320 mills on homesteads and industrial personal property, 11.6320 mills on commercial personal property, and 4.7000 mills for debt retirement. The packet also carries the April 2016 Treasurer's Report of $23,315,335.28 in total disbursements, the 2015-16 budget amendment, contract extensions for Superintendent Richard Machesky and four cabinet administrators, and a resolution urging a veto of Section 152b's $2.5 million nonpublic school appropriation.

**Meeting** — Troy School District Board of Education, regular meeting, June 21, 2016, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district masthead 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Item 2.A — Public hearing, proposed 2016/2017 budget**, presented by Rick West. Taxable value moves from a 2015 total of 3,603,511,590 to a 2016 total of 3,630,712,070 (homestead 2,458,260,260; non-homestead 1,172,451,810), annotated ".75% Increase." Proposed millage: homestead S.E.T. 6.0000, hold harmless 5.6320, debt 4.7000 (total 16.3320); non-homestead statewide 18.0000 (total 28.7). State aid assumptions: a $60 per-pupil foundation increase worth $764,400, blended enrollment of 12,740 (an increase of 24 students) worth $216,360, MPSERS categoricals held at current levels, and property value growth of approximately 0.75%. The current foundation allowance is $8,955.00 and the projected figure $9,015, with a majority of the increase arriving through a categorical because the allowance increase cannot exceed inflation.

| General Fund | Audited 6/30/2015 | Final Amd. 6/30/2016 | Original 6/30/2017 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $136,589,446 | $141,120,170 | $143,026,065 |
| Expenditures | $137,267,824 | $142,161,937 | $142,948,405 |
| Revenue (under) expenditures | ($678,378) | ($1,041,767) | $77,660 |
| Ending fund equity June 30 | $20,701,637 | $19,659,870 | $19,737,530 |
| Equity as % of expenditures | 15.08% | 13.83% | 13.81% |

Expenditure assumptions include a 2.5% increase in the PA 152 hard cap for health insurance and an MPSERS UAAL rate stabilization move from 10.53% to 11.70%, offset by an effective-rate decrease of 0.84% (25.78% to 24.94%). Salary budgets assume a net 3% increase; the General Fund receives a $650,000 transfer from the Community Service Fund.

**Item 3 — Recognitions.** Retiring School Life Troy photographer Ed Morykwas; the "2015-2016 School Year in Review" video introduced by Kerry Birmingham; Mina Mori of Troy Athens High School, honored by Brenda Carter, President-Elect of the Michigan Association of School Boards, for a Wayne State University Center for Peace and Conflict Studies study tour of Japan; eighteen Spirit of Diversity Award winners in the award's fourth year; and Dr. Richard Machesky's naming as a 2016 NSPRA "Superintendent to Watch."

**Item 6.A — Treasurer's Report, April 2016.** Total check disbursements $21,128,508.98; ACH debits $32,097.79; outgoing wire transfers $1,987,963.17; P-Card purchases $169,187.16; prior period voids ($2,421.82); total disbursements in period $23,315,335.28. Fund detail includes General Fund (101) 5,680,093.03, Special Education (122) 357,963.84, Food Service (520) 411,176.00, and Debt Funds (306, 312, 314, 315) 14,042,169.00.

**Items 7.A-7.C — Personnel.** Probationary contracts for six teachers. Superintendent Dr. Richard M. Machesky's agreement carries a $184,230 salary; the memo describes an extension through June 30, 2018 with no increase in compensation, while the attached agreement states a term of July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2019. Two-year contracts through June 30, 2018 go to Mark Dziatczak ($145,000), Rick West ($140,000), Kris Griffor ($135,000 rising to $140,000), and Jordan Harris ($140,000), each with a 3% board-funded tax-sheltered annuity.

**Item 8.A** — ELD program update from Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak, following the June 14th Board Workshop.

**Items 9.A-9.D and 11.A.** The 2015-16 amendment appropriates $142,161,937 to the General Fund and $19,540,000 to Capital Projects. The 2016-17 resolution appropriates $142,948,405 (General Fund), $8,782,050 (Special Revenue), $15,785,396 (Debt Service), $10,270,000 (2014 Capital Projects), and $2,469,355 (Capital Maintenance). Also: renewal of the Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract; authorization for ASTI to work with the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality on preservation mitigation credits for the vacant "Section 1" property on Square Lake Rd.; and the nonpublic-schools veto resolution.

**Item 3 — Recognitions.** Ed Morykwas, retiring photographer and webmaster of the monthly School Life Troy, which he helped launch two years earlier. Kerry Birmingham, Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives, introduced the "2015-2016 School Year in Review" video. Mina Mori of Troy Athens High School was honored for the Wayne State University Center for Peace and Conflict Studies program "Discovering Japan in the 21st Century: Reconciliation with the Past," which selected ten educators; she guided 11 non-Japanese speaking educators and assisted seven teachers and two board of education members for ten days in Japan, with the certificate presented by Brenda Carter, President-Elect of the Michigan Association of School Boards. The Spirit of Diversity Awards, in their fourth year and designed by the Troy Diversity & Inclusion Council, recognized eighteen individuals including the Morse Diversity and Inclusion Team, Hannah Nagi, Angelina Lai, Raje and Rahul Angamuthu, Erin Johnson and Danielle Andresen. Dr. Richard Machesky was named a 2016 "Superintendent to Watch" by the National Schools Public Relations Association, which recognizes fewer than 25 superintendents nationally.

April year-to-date reports show General Fund approved revenue $140,176,947 against actual $102,376,564 and approved expenditures $141,504,374 against actual $101,155,518, with fund balance moving from $20,701,637 on April 1 to $19,374,210 on April 30; other April 30 balances are food service $1,112,156, adult and community education $2,464,839, facilities rental $441,785, debt service $970,056 and capital projects $465,273.

**Item 7.A** recommends probationary 2016-2017 contracts for Brittany Beylerian (1st grade, Bemis), Julia Alder (Curriculum and Instruction Specialist Science), Katherine Eve (kindergarten, Hill), Katherine Kolber (1st grade, Hill), Laura Ferris (1st grade, Costello) and Lauren Brown (Special Education MoCi, Larson Middle School).

**Item 7.B — Superintendent's contract extension.** Following Dr. Rich Machesky's second-year evaluation, the memo states the contract will be extended through June 30, 2018 with no increase in compensation, while the attached Employment Agreement states a term commencing July 1, 2016 and terminating June 30, 2019 at an annual salary of $184,230. Terms include qualification under Section 1246 of the Michigan School Code of 1976 (Public Act 451 of 1976), evaluation by June 1, a 52-week work year, termination for "reasonable and good cause," 90-day non-renewal notice and American Arbitration Association arbitration in Oakland County. The Fringe Benefit Supplement provides long-term disability of 66-2/3% of monthly earnings to age 70 after 180 days, life and accidental death coverage of three times earnings up to $650,000, 25 non-carry-forward vacation days, twelve paid holidays, and unilateral compensation reductions if the audited fund balance drops below 12%. Signed by Dr. Nancy Philippart, Paula Fleming and Dr. Richard M. Machesky.

**Item 7.C** extends contracts through June 30, 2018 without tenure for Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning ($145,000); Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services ($140,000); Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Curriculum and Instruction ($135,000 for 2016-17 and $140,000 for 2017-18); and Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services ($140,000). Each adds a board-funded tax-sheltered annuity of 3% of base salary; each Schedule A provides group term life of three times earnings up to $500,000, 180 calendar days of income protection, 24 months of benefit continuation under Public Act 152 of 2011, 28 vacation days with 10 carried forward and 3 cashed out, and the same 12% fund balance clause.

**Item 8.A — ELD Program Update** by Mark Dziatczak, following the June 14th Board Workshop: renaming the program English Language Development and its staff ELD Specialists and ELD Para Educators; a Language Use Survey; a contract with Language Line Solutions; an annually reviewed EL Handbook; curriculum aligned to WIDA and Michigan State Standards with a secondary pilot; hiring of a Director of ELD, Federal Grants and State Assessments, two elementary ELD Specialists and .4 FTE secondary; W-APT testing of 300+ new K-5 students in summer 2015 expanding to grades 6-12; a 1.0 pre K-12 ELD Curriculum and Instruction Specialist in 2016; a January 2016 secondary review; and recommendations covering eSchoolPlus and/or Illuminate.

**Item 9.A — 2015-16 Budget Amendment**, appropriating General Fund $142,161,937; Food Service $3,182,130; Troy Career Center $2,103,221; Adult Education and Community Service $5,239,522; Facility Rental $1,300; Debt Service $16,635,088; Capital Projects $19,540,000; Capital Maintenance $300,000. Ending fund balances become $19,659,870 (General Fund), $1,631,810 (Food Service), $126,802 (Adult Education and Community Service, after a $2,690,000 transfer out), $1,178,387 (Debt Service), $11,706,791 (Capital Projects) and $2,469,355 (Capital Maintenance).

**Item 9.B — 2016-2017 Appropriations Resolution.** Millage: non-homestead general operating 18.0000; commercial personal property 11.6320; homestead 5.6320; all properties debt retirement 4.7000. Appropriations: General Fund $142,948,405; Special Revenue $8,782,050; Debt Service $15,785,396; 2014 Capital Projects $10,270,000; Capital Maintenance $2,469,355. General Fund revenue is $143,026,065 with total available to appropriate of $162,685,935; total instruction is $97,910,644 and total support services $44,924,494. Debt Service assumes property taxes of $18,100,000 against principal of $11,310,000 and interest of $4,428,896; Capital Projects assumes bond proceeds of $40,000,000. The Superintendent is charged with supervising execution of the budget, and the resolution takes effect immediately.

**Budget book (marked D R A F T).** Assumptions cite the 12,740 blended count, the $8,955.00 current allowance rising $60 to $9,015 largely via categorical, a retirement rate increase from 36.31% to 36.64% on October 1, 2016, a 7.65% FICA rate, premium caps at 2015 limits increased by 2.5%, a net 3% salary increase, a 6% on-schedule TESA increase with two full steps, elimination of the TESPA 4% off-schedule payment plus a 5% on-schedule step increase for tier 1 employees at step 6 or higher, and the $650,000 Community Service Fund transfer. Grants: Adult Education Civics $18,000; Adult Education Family Literacy $143,000; IDEA-Flowthrough $1,953,352; IDEA-Preschool $58,996; Michigan School Readiness $313,531; CTE Millage $110,944; Title I $600,203; Title II Part A $268,756; Title III $306,899; Workforce Investment Act $2,103,221. Enrollment headcounts run from 12,101 in September 2001 to 12,723 in September 2015 and a projected 12,740 in September 2016 (5,526 elementary, 2,948 middle, 4,266 high school). The millage history notes 31.0674 mills for operating purposes in 1993/94 and that rates will be finalized with the L-4029 (Treasury Form 614, due September 30, 2016). Debt amortization totals principal of $111,925,000.00 and interest of $30,015,849.00.

**Items 9.C, 9.D and 11.A.** Renewal of the food service contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2016/2017, originally approved June 2, 2015 and already approved by the Michigan Department of Education. For the vacant "Section 1" property on Square Lake Rd. between John R. and Dequindre, the Board was asked to authorize ASTI to work with the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality on preservation mitigation credits, as a Capital Maintenance Fund expenditure. A final resolution urges the Governor to veto Section 152b of the School Aid Budget and its $2.5 million allocation for nonpublic schools as likely violating Article VIII Sec. 2 of the Michigan Constitution, "PASSED and APPROVED this 21st day of June, 2016," signed by Nancy Philippart, President, and Paula Fleming, Secretary.
